![](/static/diagrams/15-assurance-level-decision.png){fig-alt="A four step diagram. Step one scores six impact dimensions, step two scores six likelihood dimensions, step three reads the level off a four by four matrix, step four says what each level asks for. Every combination in the matrix is described in the text below the picture."}

<details>
<summary>Text description of this diagram</summary>

**Step 1. Score the impact of an error, and take the highest.** The six impact dimensions are
Decision, Finance, Customers, Legal or compliance, Public visibility and reach, and Reputation.
Each scores 1 for low or informational, 2 for moderate or operational, 3 for high or
organisational, and 4 for very high or business critical. Any one dimension at 4 is Business
Critical: it does not need two, and it carries the analysis to Level 4 whatever the likelihood.

**Step 2. Score the likelihood of an error, and take the highest.** The six likelihood dimensions
are Data complexity, Analytical complexity, Assumptions and proxies and judgement, Novelty, Manual
intervention or automated, and Documentation and reproducibility. Each scores 1 for a low risk of
error up to 4 for very high.

**Step 3. Read the level off the matrix.** The matrix is four impact rows by four likelihood
columns.

| Impact | Likelihood 1 | Likelihood 2 | Likelihood 3 | Likelihood 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **4** | Level 4 BCA | Level 4 BCA | Level 4 BCA | Level 4 BCA |
| **3** | Level 1 Standard | Level 2 Enhanced | Level 3 Comprehensive | Level 3 Comprehensive |
| **2** | Level 1 Standard | Level 2 Enhanced | Level 2 Enhanced | Level 3 Comprehensive |
| **1** | Level 1 Standard | Level 1 Standard | Level 1 Standard | Level 2 Enhanced |

Every cell in the top row is Level 4, which is the same rule as step 1.

**Step 4. Do what the level asks.** Level 1 Standard is routine work whose consequences are
contained. Level 2 Enhanced is work that matters operationally, or is harder to get right. Level 3
Comprehensive is work that carries organisational consequence. Level 4 BCA is Business Critical,
where consequences are large and external. Each level adds to the one below it, and section 6
lists every check and the level at which it is first required.

**What does not, by itself, make analysis Business Critical.** "Publication status, Board
consideration, Official Statistics designation, media interest, national visibility, FOI
disclosure, ministerial interest or parliamentary scrutiny do not by themselves justify a Level 4
score."

**Where NHSBSA has placed its own work**, from the worked examples annex to the decision sheet,
which the workbook marks as still to be developed. Level 1 Standard: exploratory analysis,
internal data investigation. Level 2 Enhanced: monthly operational dashboard, team workforce
planning. Level 3 Comprehensive: Prescription Cost Analysis, Dental Statistics, FOI response,
Board report, ministerial briefing. Level 4 BCA: funding allocation formula, eligibility model.

</details>
